name: Publish with Akana page and enquiry form
what: Public page for authors and publishing houses: what Akana does, the three acquisition models, the white-label option, and an enquiry form that writes to a leads table and emails Crent. Process only, no revenue figures until Crent sets them.
why: Outreach starts now and needs a page to point at before the portal exists.
risk: Publishing terms or rates before they are decided. Page stays on process.

name: Marketing home page
what: Home with the line 'the place where books become practical', how it works in three steps, featured shelves, membership offer, local prices, trust points (official author-licensed workbooks, no ad pixels, what we never collect). Reduced-motion cover hero.
why: Front door for readers and the first thing an author judges.
risk: Copy drifting into outcome claims. Runs through the claims check.

name: Library with genre shelves and Themes
what: Public library across the eleven genres with Themes grouped under genre shelves. Filter chips for genre, Theme, author, language, programme length, Mine and In progress. Cards show title-first identity: book title, author, Theme chip, card line, badge. A shelf stays hidden until it reaches a minimum count Crent sets.
why: Browsing is the main way in with 50 or more titles and 17 or more authors. It must look like a multi-author store on day one.
risk: Wellbeing and finance Themes side by side read oddly. Group Themes under genre.

name: Badges and demo labelling on every surface
what: One badge per workbook from licence_ref: Official, Made with the author, Public domain classic (edition and translator named), Demo. Demo shows on card, page, author page, search, player header and checkout. Checkout refuses a demo id.
why: Selling invented authors as real would mislead buyers. The Official badge is the pitch, so it must be accurate.
risk: A demo title slipping into live paid listings. Build check and checkout both refuse.

name: Public workbook pages on slug URLs
what: Server-rendered page per workbook at /w/{slug}: cover, title, author, code, badge, card line, who it is for, week-by-week outline, a readable sample of the first exercise, time per day, language, price in local currency, buy and membership buttons, links to buy the book through /go/, Help now link on wellbeing titles. schema.org Book and Product with no health claims. 301 on retitle. Hidden topics never in page text or metadata.
why: This is the page that sells and the page authors share.
risk: Hidden topics leaking into metadata. A build check fails on any topic word.
status_note: The /w/[slug] page, outline, sample and schema.org data are built; there is no 301 on retitle and no price or buy buttons until prices are set.

name: Author and publisher pages
what: /author/{slug} and /publisher/{slug}: display name (pen name, never legal name), photo, short bio, country, their workbooks and books, link to their own site. Demo label on demo authors and in metadata.
why: Seventeen named authors is the marketplace's proof, and the URL authors will share.
risk: Invented authors that look real. Demo label on page and in metadata.

name: Theme pages
what: /t/{slug} per Theme with its plain line and every workbook on it from any author. Email links land here because emails never name a title.
why: Themes are the shared positive shelves and the landing point for email.
risk: Theme names not trademark cleared (gate T1). Renameable through the registry.

name: On-device search with Help now first
what: Search over a catalogue index built at deploy and searched in the browser: title, author, publisher, Theme, code, shelf and hidden topics. No query sent or stored. Crisis words show a Help now card above results.
why: Positive Theme names are hard to guess. Private search is a published promise.
risk: Crisis word list awaits clinician sign-off (gate C1). Ship the interim list. A server search later would break the promise; the privacy notice must cover both cases.

name: For publishers, white-label and pricing pages
what: Pages for publishers (marketplace), white-label (own branded site), and reader pricing. Plan names and prices only once Crent sets them; until then 'talk to us'.
why: Crent is selling both models now.
risk: Quoting plan prices before they exist.

name: Help centre and FAQ
what: Static help pages for readers (access, refunds, deletion, Help now) and a link to the support address. Marked as not a crisis service.
why: Cuts support load and is expected in any paid product.
risk: Low.

name: Sitemap, Open Graph and hreflang
what: Sitemap, robots, Open Graph share images per workbook and author, canonical tags, hreflang for en-GB and en-US.
why: Authors share links; a bare preview looks unfinished.
risk: Low.
status_note: Sitemap, robots, canonical links and en-GB and en-US alternates are built; no Open Graph share images exist.

name: Reader ratings and reviews (parked)
what: Star ratings or written reviews on workbook pages, pre-moderated, possibly non-wellbeing only.
why: Earlier board banned ratings on wellbeing titles as an effectiveness claim. Reviews bring health disclosures, moderation and wider Online Safety Act and DSA duties. Commercial wants social proof.
risk: Not planned. Needs Crent's decision and a lawyer's view.

name: Headless CMS for marketing content
what: Blog, campaigns and landing pages in a CMS. At launch, pages come from the catalogue plus MDX in the repo.
why: Only needed once someone other than Crent edits the site.
risk: Low.

name: Reader app shell with tenant design tokens
what: One Next.js App Router project for site, library and player. Five-tab reader nav carried over (Home, Today, Toolkit, Library, You). Design tokens from index.html moved into CSS variables using logical properties, read per tenant from the host, defaulting to Akana.
why: Everything else sits inside it. Tokens now cost a day; retrofitting later costs a week.
risk: Creep into a full design system. Tokens plus the components ported from the current app only.

name: Workbook player port with a parity harness
what: Port the engine in app/src/index.html to React client components reading the same JSON: all field types now used, stages and weeks, short versions, Start screen with 'I have read this', toolkit and breathing pacer, daily check, weekly check-in, unscored self-checks, milestones, autosave with 'Saved'. Logic lifted, not rewritten. A harness loads every workbook JSON, renders every screen and fails on any field it cannot draw. Old app stays live until parity.
why: This is the product. The current engine is about 180 KB in one file, so it is a port with hidden edge cases.
risk: Largest single item; starts day 1 and is due end of Week 2. Field types first, Maya Vaughn 20 through the harness daily. Fallback if it slips past day 10: mount the old engine as a client island and port screen by screen after launch.

name: Today and Home across several workbooks
what: A continue card per active workbook, capped with the rest under Library. One reminder. The daily check appears only for workbooks that have one, so a finance reader never gets a mood question.
why: Membership makes several open workbooks across genres the normal case.
risk: Clutter. Cap shown cards.

name: My plan, prefill and finish sequence
what: Generalise prefill_from so earlier answers carry into My plan in every workbook, each line tagged by week and editable. Keep going mode after the last week. Finish screen names the book and author and links to buy it through /go/.
why: My plan is the payoff. The finish screen is the author's main reward.
risk: A prefilled line the reader no longer agrees with. Every line editable.

name: Progress without streaks
what: Weeks done, current step, milestones, My plan lines, a plain list of recent daily checks with blank days neutral. No streaks, missed-day counts or comparison.
why: Readers want to see where they are. House rules forbid punishing streaks.
risk: Commercial pressure to add streaks. The rule stands.

name: Free first week and calm paywall
what: Week 1 open after sign-up with no card. Week 2 onwards shows a calm paywall with buy and membership. Answers carry into the paid workbook. Per-workbook flag, on by default.
why: Market standard, already built, and the conversion step without pressure.
risk: Free weeks across 50 titles add up. Crent may cap free weeks per reader.

name: Completed-step event capture
what: Record step completed and week opened as ids and timestamps only, per reader, workbook and version, from day one. Feeds the subscription pool and funnel.
why: The first pool cannot be calculated fairly later if the events were not captured at launch.
risk: An event carrying an answer or a feeling. Ids and timestamps only.

name: Safety hub and Help now by market
what: Carry over hubHTML, markets.json and support_lines.json. Help now one tap away on every screen of a wellbeing workbook, by region, with the verified date. Helpline finder for markets outside the six. Non-wellbeing titles get a quiet 'Need support?' footer link.
why: Standing rule. A multi-country catalogue brings readers from many countries.
risk: A stale number. Rebuilt from JSON every deploy; weekly link checker kept.

name: Safety tier gating and the hardest answer card
what: Each workbook carries a safety tier (none, standard, higher). Higher tier keeps the Start screen and needs a recorded clinical sign-off before going live. Unified hardest-answer card at most weekly, never alerting anyone.
why: Wellness not treatment applies to every author's workbook.
risk: A parenting or relationships title touching abuse or self-harm tagged non-wellbeing. Akana sets tier at review, never the author.

name: Export of the reader's own work
what: JSON export and a print-ready page of prompts, answers and My plan, printed to PDF from the browser. Gated by emailed code, passkey optional. Neutral header unless the reader ticks Show the book title. Exports prompts and answers, not the teaching text. Server-side PDF with a name watermark follows after launch.
why: UK GDPR portability and market standard. Already built in the old app.
risk: Server-side PDF on Vercel needs fonts and a print layout per field type. Fallback is print-to-PDF from the browser.
status_note: JSON and printable exports with the plain header are built; the emailed code gate is not.

name: Calendar reminder
what: Downloadable calendar reminder with neutral text ('Daily check' or 'Workbook time'), never a title or Theme.
why: Reminders without push permission or a server job. Already built.
risk: Low.

name: You tab: account, settings and data rights
what: My library (owned, membership, in progress, finished), region and currency, appearance settings carried over, email preferences, receipts, export, and deletion with the 7-day undo. Deletion cascades through answers, entitlements, tenant memberships and Stripe customer metadata, keeping only the financial records tax law requires.
why: Readers must find what they paid for and leave cleanly. UK and EU law gives them most of this.
risk: Deleting tax records that must be kept. Financial records held apart and named in the privacy notice.
status_note: Membership, appearance, export, consents and deletion with the 7-day undo are on You; no My library list, region or currency choice, email preferences or receipts.

name: Health data consent screen
what: Explicit, versioned consent before a reader's first wellbeing workbook. News opt-in carried over.
why: Wellbeing answers are health data.
risk: Consent text not reviewed. Reuse the reviewed version from the current build.

name: Discreet tab title and hide covers
what: Plain tab title and covers hidden on Home, as a setting. Copy says it stops a glance only.
why: Title-first identity makes screens more revealing. The small part is cheap; app lock is not.
risk: Readers reading 'discreet' as 'secure'.

name: App lock with passkey
what: Optional app lock reusing passkeys, Help now reachable from the lock screen.
why: Matters most for higher-tier titles, which stay paused until clinician sign-off.
risk: Low.

name: Interactive signed-out first exercise
what: Answer the first exercise without an account; answers held in the browser and moved into sealed storage on sign-up. At launch the public page shows a readable sample only.
why: Value before sign-up. Hidden work moving local answers safely and clearing them on shared devices.
risk: Wellbeing answers left in a shared browser.

name: Check-in partner
what: Built 7 October 2026 (Day 6), ahead of plan. Migration 0012, the /respond/[token] route and a Check-in partner section on the You page. A reader has one partner with no account, who acts only through single-purpose hashed token links. Share level 1 sends the stage reached by number, level 2 adds a gentle question, level 3 adds a short note the reader writes. Wellbeing progress is shared only if the reader ticks it. Partners never see answers, workbook titles or stage names. Invitations and updates are rate limited in the database, and audit rows never hold a name, address or note.
why: Carried over from the old app, where readers valued it. It is now built, so it moves from after launch into the shipped set. Its token and rate-limit pattern is reused by Akana Business invitations (F-203) and group check-ins (F-213).
risk: Partner mail naming a workbook or a stage. The email render test applies. The level 3 note is reader-written text sent to another person; the lawyer should confirm it stays outside the Online Safety Act user-to-user scope [check legal].

name: Hard-day mode, cross-workbook toolkit, read aloud
what: Short version plus one tool and Help now; one Toolkit across owned workbooks; on-device read aloud.
why: Retention features from the old roadmap.
risk: Low.
status_note: The Toolkit tab gathers tools from every open workbook; hard-day mode and read aloud are not built.

name: Native app store wrappers (parked)
what: App Store and Google Play wrappers.
why: Store fees and store health-claim review. The web avoids both.
risk: Not planned.

name: Invite-only author and publisher onboarding
what: Akana staff create the organisation and send an invite. The invitee signs in with magic link or passkey and lands on a first-run checklist: profile, add a book, sign licence, set up payouts, submit. No open public sign-up at launch.
why: Leanest route to real authors. Open sign-up brings fraud screening and likely Online Safety Act and DSA marketplace duties.
risk: Manual invites do not scale past a few dozen. Fine for launch.

name: Author profile editor
what: Display name (pen name) and legal name held apart, short bio, photo with a rights tick, country, website, links. Bio runs the claim-word check; staff approve before it goes public.
why: Regulators read intended purpose from all marketing, including bios on Akana's site.
risk: False positives. Show the flagged phrase; staff override with a logged reason.

name: Book records with contributors and editions
what: Book record separate from the workbook: title, subtitle, series, contributors with roles (author, translator, editor) and death years, edition, ISBN or ASIN, publisher, imprint, year, language, genre, cover with rights tick, store link, KDP Select declaration. One book can have several workbooks.
why: Title-first identity hangs off the book. Translators matter for public-domain traps.
risk: Duplicate book records. ISBN uniqueness check; merge tool after launch.

name: Licence capture by clickwrap or signed upload
what: Per book, accept a versioned interactive workbook licence with plain heads of terms, variable terms (territory, term, exclusivity, subscription inclusion, cover and audio rights, what buyers keep), warranties (rights held, no publisher or KDP Select clash, no health claims in own marketing). Stores version, signer, time and IP as licence_ref. Also accepts an uploaded signed PDF for houses that insist on paper. Build refuses to set a workbook live without it.
why: No in-copyright workbook can be sold without a written licence (board decision 8).
risk: The licence text is the blocker, not the code (gate L3). Code ships with placeholder text marked draft; no real author signs until L3 clears.

name: Workbook submission: upload or request Akana development
what: Route one: upload manuscript and any existing workbook (DOCX, EPUB, PDF) to a private bucket with a short brief; Akana editors build the JSON. Route two: request Akana development, receive a quote, pay a deposit by Stripe payment link or invoice. Both create a Draft workbook.
why: How real workbooks reach the platform in three weeks with a small team.
risk: Editor capacity becomes the bottleneck [check team size]. Manuscripts are unpublished IP: private bucket, no public URLs, never used for training.

name: Preview in the real reader engine
what: Open any draft in the actual player in preview mode: Demo watermark, no purchase, answers not saved server side. Phone and desktop, both themes, 200% text. Org members only.
why: Authors will not sign off what they cannot see as readers see it.
risk: Preview drifting from live. One renderer.

name: Author review, comments and sign-off
what: Author sees status, the single comment thread per workbook, and approves short title, card line and the Made with the author badge, then signs off against an exact content hash. Safety lines and Help now are locked against author edits.
why: Sign-off on an exact version is what makes the release gate mean anything.
risk: Reviewers re-read whole workbooks without diffs. Fine at launch volumes.

name: Pricing from the Akana ladder
what: Author picks from a fixed GBP ladder with preset local prices, chooses subscription inclusion if the licence allows, and sees an estimate of their share net of VAT and fees. Akana approves with the workbook and creates the Stripe prices.
why: Free-text prices break the store, the currency tables and pool maths. Net estimates stop disputes about what a share means.
risk: Ladder and share figures not set. Built as config with placeholders marked as such.

name: Earnings and statements view
what: Org sees its ledger lines and monthly statements per workbook, with the method stated in plain words. No reader identity.
why: Authors and their accountants need a statement they can check.
risk: Net receipts definition must match the licence exactly.

name: Privacy-safe sales and engagement dashboard
what: Monthly counts per workbook: listing views, free weeks started, purchases, readers finishing week one and the final week. Counts under 10 show as 'Fewer than 10'; no daily view; filters cannot combine below the threshold; country is the finest location. Never answers, check-ins or how readers felt. Simple tables, CSV.
why: Authors promote only if they can see results. Strong point in outreach.
risk: Exact earnings can back out small counts. Crent to decide whether earnings are thresholded.

name: Author status and payout emails
what: Invite, submission received, changes requested, ready for sign-off, live, paused, payout action needed, statement ready. Separate template set from reader mail; author mail may name the workbook.
why: Authors lose trust when nothing seems to move.
risk: Confusion with the reader rule. Separate set keeps the reader render test intact.

name: Author help pages and house rules
what: Short help on house rules in plain words, review timeline, pricing rules, how payment works, what the pool will be.
why: Authors from many countries will not know why a bio was flagged or why scores are not allowed.
risk: Low.

name: Demo author login and seeded portal states
what: A resettable demo author and demo publisher login for sales calls, with workbooks in every state (draft, in review, live, paused), test-mode sales, a sample statement and a populated dashboard, all labelled Demo.
why: Crent sells by showing. An empty portal does not sell.
risk: Demo figures confused with real results. Test mode only and labelled everywhere.

name: Author referral link attribution
what: /from/{slug}?a={org} records author-referred sales in checkout metadata with a first-party cookie. Rate application waits on Crent's two-rate decision.
why: Capturing attribution from day one is cheap; applying a second rate is a ledger rule later.
risk: Attribution disputes. Publish the window rule.

name: No-code workbook builder
what: Form editor over schema v3: listing, weeks, steps, exercises from allowed field types, toolkit, milestones, live validation, safety blocks locked, no scores or self-harm questions offered.
why: Scales the catalogue without staff. One side argued it pays for the demo content; the other that Akana builds first workbooks anyway and it is XL.
risk: Author-built content moves Akana toward a marketplace model with different Online Safety Act, DSA and P2B position. Legal view first.

name: DOCX and EPUB import to draft
what: Mammoth DOCX import and EPUB reading order to a draft outline and JSON, every exercise citing its manuscript location. Word template with Akana styles.
why: Speeds editors at volume. First authors are built by hand.
risk: Invented content. Citation rule and validator guard.

name: Machine-assisted draft from manuscript
what: Generate outline, exercise map and draft JSON with citations from an uploaded manuscript, always through full review.
why: A library of thousands cannot be built by hand.
risk: Invented content. Needs licence cover for adaptation.

name: Author promo codes
what: Author-created discount codes within Akana limits, backed by Stripe promotion codes. Staff create codes by hand at launch.
why: Useful for launches, not needed to take first money.
risk: Leaks to deal sites. Caps and expiry by default.

name: Co-authors and split payees
what: Several payees per workbook with percentage splits. One payee per workbook is a stated licence term until then.
why: Real but uncommon at launch.
risk: Low.

name: Line comments and version diffs in review
what: Comments on a line and diffs since the reviewer's last sign-off.
why: Cuts review time at volume.
risk: Low.

name: Reader to author messaging (not planned)
what: No direct messages. An author welcome letter and end-of-week notes ship as reviewed workbook content instead.
why: Messages about wellbeing are health data and make Akana a user-to-user service.
risk: Authors will ask. The answer is the dashboard and the referral link.

name: SAML sign-in for publisher staff
what: SAML through Supabase SSO for large organisations.
why: Large houses ask in procurement.
risk: A named prospect may require it to sign [check].

name: Organisation console with members and invites
what: One console for publishers, solo authors and tenants: invite, resend, revoke, change role, remove a member with session revocation. An organisation always keeps one owner, enforced in the database. Ownership transfer by staff at launch.
why: Publishers must give staff access without sharing a login, and a departed employee must lose payout access.
risk: Last owner leaves. Database rule.

name: Author roster and imprints as labels
what: An organisation lists its authors (profiles without logins unless invited) and imprints. Imprint is a label and a statement filter, not a permission boundary.
why: Title-first identity needs the author on every card; publishers think in imprints.
risk: Low.

name: CSV catalogue import
what: CSV template for book and listing metadata with row-by-row validation and a dry run. Creates drafts only; licence gate still applies.
why: A backlist cannot be keyed by hand. CSV covers launch prospects; ONIX follows.
risk: Bad cover URLs and rights mismatches. Draft-only.

name: Publisher statements and sales roll-up
what: Statements and the privacy-safe dashboard rolled up across imprints and authors, filterable by imprint, CSV export.
why: No publisher signs without statements they can reconcile.
risk: Pool rule undecided, so subscription lines show as pending.

name: Organisation audit log view
what: Owners see who changed prices, listings, roles, payout details and domains.
why: Disputes over prices and payouts need a record.
risk: Low.

name: Bulk catalogue tools
what: Change price, Theme, availability or subscription inclusion across many titles with preview and undo.
why: Routine publisher work once catalogues grow.
risk: Bulk publish must respect each title's review gate.

name: ONIX import and translated editions
what: ONIX feed import [check version] and translated workbooks linked to the original, each with its own safety review and local Help now.
why: Larger houses will not enter backlists by hand.
risk: Each language needs its own clinical and legal review.

name: Catalogue potential finder
what: Admin uploads a backlist CSV and gets a rubric-scored shortlist with editable reasons, as a PDF for a sales meeting. No sales forecasts. Done by hand with Claude until built.
why: Turns the 'unused potential' pitch into a deliverable.
risk: Must never show invented figures.

name: Per-author payouts inside a publisher
what: Split a publisher's royalties to its authors' Connect accounts.
why: Publishers already pay their own authors.
risk: More Connect accounts and fees.

name: Publisher API and sales webhooks
what: Read-only API and webhooks for sales and statement data.
why: Larger houses will ask once volume exists.
risk: Low.

name: Self-billing statements for VAT-registered publishers
what: Statements issued as self-billed VAT invoices under a self-billing agreement [check accountant].
why: UK publishers charge VAT on royalties. Needed before the first VAT-registered publisher payout, not before launch.
risk: Easy to miss until a finance team asks.

name: Tenant resolution by hostname and cookie isolation
what: Proxy reads the host, looks up the tenant (Edge Config cache) and serves its catalogue and branding. Tenant subdomains on a separate apex from Akana's own, submitted to the Public Suffix List. __Host- cookies with no Domain attribute, Origin checks. Admin and auth stay on the Akana apex.
why: This is the white-label product, and the leak that would end it.
risk: Public Suffix List inclusion takes time [check]. Cookie rules must hold on their own until then.
status_note: Host resolution from a config map is live; the database lookup sits behind TENANT_DB_LOOKUP=1, with no Edge Config cache and no tenant apex chosen (A7).

name: Tenant branding with contrast check
what: Logo, favicon, two brand colours, a font from a fixed list, footer links, legal page links, sender name. Colours validated against WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes before save. 'Powered by Akana' by plan.
why: Brand is what a white-label buyer pays for. Contrast checking keeps tenants inside EAA duties they mostly carry.
risk: A tenant wanting full CSS. No at launch.

name: Locked standards on tenant sites
what: Help now, safety lines and the wellness-not-treatment notice cannot be hidden or restyled. No custom script or pixel injection. Tenant wellbeing titles pass Akana's safety review. Emails never name a title on any tenant.
why: A tenant site is Akana software; a safety failure there is Akana's.
risk: Tenants asking for analytics. Offer aggregate exports.

name: Tenant catalogue and own prices
what: Tenant picks which licensed workbooks appear and sets its own prices from the ladder in GBP and fixed local currencies. Same pages, outline and free week, in tenant branding.
why: Own pricing is the second publisher ask in research. Reuses marketplace pages.
risk: Tenant subscriptions need their own pool. Single sales only on tenants at launch.
status_note: Tenant catalogue and prices are stored as settings; tenant hosts cannot sign in, read or buy until shared identity (F-133) and tenant checkout (F-070).

name: Tenant checkout on the shared payment path
what: Stripe Checkout on the tenant's site using the marketplace code path: destination charge to the tenant's Connect account with Akana's application fee, tenant name on receipts, entitlement written with tenant_id.
why: Taking money on a tenant site in three weeks is only realistic by reusing one flow. The other side: direct charges make the publisher seller of record and keep Akana out of VAT on tenant sales.
risk: With destination charges Akana is seller of record and owes VAT on tenant sales. Depends on Crent's merchant-of-record answer. Cut from the three weeks: target is the first signed tenant, about two weeks after launch.

name: Custom domain, admin assisted
what: Akana admin adds a tenant domain through the Vercel API (add, TXT check, verify) with a status line the tenant sees. SSL automatic.
why: Own domain is the main reason to buy white-label. Admin-assisted is a fraction of the build.
risk: DNS support. Clear status screen. Cut from the three weeks: target is the first signed tenant, about two weeks after launch.

name: Tenant Site tab in the organisation console
what: Branding, domain status, catalogue toggles, prices, plan and billing, members and audit log in one tab. No separate admin product.
why: Tenants run their site without emailing Akana.
risk: Scope creep. This list only. Cut from the three weeks: target is the first signed tenant, about two weeks after launch.

name: Tenant plans on Stripe Billing with plan flags
what: Starter and Pro as Stripe Billing subscriptions, Enterprise invoiced by hand. One table maps plan to limits (titles, domains, seats, branding removal); admins override per org. Stripe portal and default dunning. Suspension stops admin and new sales, never readers' paid access.
why: The white-label tier earns nothing until tenants can be billed.
risk: Prices not set. Plan flags let prices change without code. Cut from the three weeks: target is the first signed tenant, about two weeks after launch.

name: Seeded demo publisher and demo tenant site
what: One invented publisher with two imprints and demo authors, and one demo tenant on its own subdomain with distinct branding, all marked Demo, with a reset script.
why: A working branded site beside the marketplace is the demo that closes a publisher.
risk: Demo data in real statements. Flagged and excluded from every ledger.

name: Direct charges with publisher as merchant of record
what: Second payment mode where sales land on the tenant's own Stripe account and the tenant carries VAT, refunds and disputes.
why: Larger publishers may insist on being seller of record.
risk: Splits refund, tax and entitlement logic into two paths.

name: Self-serve tenant sign-up, domains and email domain
what: Public plan sign-up with trial, self-serve domain entry, sending from the tenant's own domain.
why: Growth features while sales are founder-led.
risk: Unvetted tenants publishing unsafe wellbeing content. Review gate stays.

name: Tenant data export and offboarding
what: CSV of orders and consented contacts, termination flow covering what readers keep and domain release. Never answers.
why: Standard procurement ask. The DPA covers it contractually at launch.
risk: Consent scope must be clear.

name: Tenant titles also listed on the marketplace
what: Toggle to list tenant workbooks on Akana, with a rule on reader ownership and rate.
why: Cross-sell, but needs Crent's commercial rule.
risk: Channel conflict.

name: Per-tenant manifest, SEO and accessibility statement
what: Manifest, icons, sitemap and Open Graph per tenant; generated accessibility statement per tenant.
why: A branded site that installs under the Akana name looks unfinished.
risk: Service worker scope per host needs testing.

name: Staff roles and admin access
what: Staff roles in app_metadata: owner, editor, safety reviewer, support, finance. Admin on its own route on the Akana apex, never a tenant host. Passkey or TOTP required. is_staff(role) checked on every admin call. No role can see reader answers.
why: Every other admin feature needs to know who is acting.
risk: A staff account takeover. MFA and short sessions; answers out of reach.

name: Append-only audit log
what: Widen admin_access_log into one append-only log for staff and org actions: who, role, action, target, reason (picklist plus note), time. Insert only, no update or delete grant.
why: Takedowns, refunds, payout holds and price changes all need a record.
risk: Must never log answers or health data.

name: Create and approve organisations
what: Staff create an organisation, set type and plan, invite the owner, attach contract records, see Connect and terms status, suspend a payee or tenant.
why: Akana curates, so every organisation is approved before it sells.
risk: Admin bottleneck past a few dozen orgs.

name: Kill switch and pause controls
what: Pause one exercise, a workbook, an author's catalogue or a tenant within minutes through a server flag read on every content fetch. Paused content leaves sale; owners keep their own answers. Every pause logged with a reason.
why: Response to a wrong support line, takedown, licence dispute or suspension.
risk: Pool maths across pause windows. Ledger records them.
status_note: Pause and resume work per workbook with an audited reason (0008); pausing one exercise, an author's catalogue or a tenant is not built.

name: Review queue with statuses and validator results
what: One status per workbook version: draft, submitted, editorial, safety review, clinical sign-off (higher tier only), author sign-off, live, paused, retired. Queue lists assignee, age and validator result. Reviewers comment, send back with reasons, or advance. One email to the assignee.
why: Curation keeps Akana publisher of provider content and the house rules intact across many authors.
risk: Crent as sole reviewer becomes the bottleneck. Simple enough for a second editor on day one.

name: Release gate with sign-off records
what: Go-live refused unless the version passed the validator and has editor, author or publisher, and (wellbeing) safety reviewer sign-offs against its content hash, plus a licence or public-domain record. Higher tier also needs a named clinician record. Override needs two named staff, logged.
why: Today nothing technical stops unsigned content reaching readers.
risk: Without a clinician (gate C1) higher-tier titles cannot launch. Intended, not a bug.

name: Staff workbook JSON editor with live validation
what: In-admin editor for workbook JSON with schema hints and live validator output, saving a new draft version. Replaces the no-code builder at launch.
why: Editors need to fix and build workbooks without a deploy, and the builder is cut.
risk: Hand-edited JSON errors. Validator blocks save on errors.

name: Account lookup console with four actions
what: Look up a reader by email (entitlements, orders, subscription, email log, deletion status) or an organisation (Connect status, workbooks, ledger totals). Actions: refund, resend a service email, restore access, cancel a deletion. Reason required, every lookup logged. No route to answers.
why: Without it every support case is raw SQL on live data.
risk: Creep into an edit-anything admin. Four actions only.

name: Owner dashboards from saved views
what: Extend db/008 owner views to many authors and tenants: funnel by workbook, author and genre; revenue gross, VAT, fees, net; refunds; royalties owed and paid. owner.sup() hides 1 to 4. Tables, no charts. Excludes demo and test mode.
why: Crent needs to see whether it sells.
risk: Demo or test orders in the numbers.
status_note: /admin/funnel shows counts by workbook and /admin/money shows ledger balances; no revenue, VAT, fee or royalty views by author or genre.

name: Support line freshness list
what: Every line in support_lines.json with its verified date; lines past a set age show as due; staff record a new check.
why: A wrong number is the most serious content fault. Data already exists.
risk: Low.

name: Support inbox on an existing tool with saved replies
what: Route the support address to an existing inbox (Resend inbound or a basic helpdesk) [check fit], with saved replies for refunds, access, deletion, payouts and 'I am worried about someone'. Auto-reply says it is not a crisis service.
why: A human route is needed before the first live payment. Building a helpdesk is waste.
risk: Provider holds messages with health information. DPA needed, no tracking.

name: Data subject request list
what: Staff list of open deletion and access requests with statutory due dates.
why: Reader flows are automatic; staff only need visibility.
risk: Low.
status_note: Staff can read deletion requests in the database (0007) and see deletion state in the account lookup; there is no request list with statutory due dates.

name: Stripe platform account, Tax and Connect enabled
what: Platform account in live and test mode, Stripe Tax on, Connect platform profile submitted, Radar defaults, webhook endpoints. Product names generic ('Akana workbook') so bank statements never name a title.
why: Nothing sells without it, and Connect approval can take time.
risk: Connect platform review time [check]. Submit on day one.
status_note: Stripe sandbox has the webhooks, Connect platform and products; Stripe Tax is off, no live account is set up and Radar rules are defaults.

name: Price ladder and Stripe price catalogue
what: GBP ladder with fixed EUR, USD, AUD, CAD and NZD prices per point, membership monthly and annual, held as config and Stripe price ids. Tax-inclusive display where that is the rule.
why: One source for every displayed and charged price.
risk: Figures not set by Crent. Placeholders marked.
status_note: Ladder rows exist with empty amounts and membership has interim prices; Crent has not set the figures (D1 to D4).

name: Local currency price display
what: Price chosen from region with a manual switch, read from the same Stripe price ids the checkout uses. Adaptive Pricing elsewhere.
why: GBP leads; readers abroad will not buy in a currency they cannot read.
risk: Shown price differing from checkout. Same ids.
status_note: Shows the reader's own currency where a price exists, otherwise GBP with a note; no manual currency switch.

name: Entitlements engine
what: One table and one check for free week, purchase for life, membership, tenant access (gift and team seat types reserved). Lapsed membership becomes read only. Buyers keep access when a licence ends. Content served a week at a time only to entitled readers.
why: Every screen asks 'can this reader open this'.
risk: The old 'whole library for life' tier may not survive a multi-author store. Crent to decide.

name: Single workbook checkout and webhook
what: Stripe Checkout in payment mode with Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link, Stripe Tax, promotion codes, tax ID field. Immediate-access consent with version [check legal] alongside the pro rata refund promise. Destination charge to the payee's Connect account where verified. Webhook grants access idempotently; success page reconciles and drops the reader into Week 1. Demo ids refused.
why: The minimum to take real money.
risk: Webhook failure leaving a paid reader locked out. Reconcile on the success page; alert on failures.
status_note: Checkout, consent and webhook are built in test mode and refuse until prices exist; the author share is paid by later transfers, not a destination charge.

name: Membership subscription and self-service
what: Monthly and annual membership in subscription mode with the auto-renewal consent. Stripe customer portal for cancel, card change and invoices. Renewal reminder before annual renewal, failed-payment email and grace period. Cancellation as easy as sign-up.
why: The business case leans on subscription income.
risk: Membership on sale before authors know how the pool pays. Reader side ships; pool rule must be in the licence before outreach.

name: Receipts without titles in email
what: Email receipts show the plan or AK code only. Full receipt with title, VAT breakdown and Akana's VAT number in the account and as a PDF.
why: Reconciles 'emails never name a title' with VAT receipt rules.
risk: A code-only email may not be a valid VAT invoice [check accountant].
status_note: Emails carry the plan or AK code only; there is no full receipt with VAT number in the account or as a PDF.

name: Connect Express onboarding for organisation payees
what: Org owner or finance completes Stripe-hosted Express onboarding. Console shows not started, pending, verified, action needed. Captures tax residence and treaty declaration. Paid workbooks cannot go live until verified, except Akana-owned and public-domain titles. Payees outside the self-serve cross-border list are told plainly and held as payout pending.
why: No author signs without a clear route to being paid.
risk: From a UK platform, self-serve payouts reach the US, UK, EEA, Canada and Switzerland only (research_money). Authors in India, Nigeria, Brazil and elsewhere need Global Payouts or Stripe sales.

name: Royalty ledger on net receipts
what: Append-only ledger written by the webhook: one row per sale, refund, dispute and payout with gross, VAT, Stripe fee, net, Akana share, author share, currency and the rate stored on the line. Refunds reverse the Connect transfer. Demo and test mode never enter. Daily reconciliation to Stripe balance transactions.
why: Research found the summary counted VAT as revenue and left out fees. Paying on net from day one avoids paying on money Akana never kept.
risk: Refund after transfer leaves negative balances. Carried forward; tested before launch.

name: Monthly statements PDF and CSV
what: Statement per organisation and month: units, gross, deductions, net and rate per title, method in plain words. Closes after the refund window.
why: A statement they cannot reconcile kills the relationship.
risk: Rounding and FX drift. Minor units and FX rate stored per line.

name: Refunds from the console
what: Refund button that calls Stripe, applies the billing.ts rule (pro rata on passes in the window, reopens after annual renewal), handles single purchases under Crent's policy, reverses the author transfer and sends the refund email. Partial refunds.
why: Taking money requires a working refund path on day one.
risk: Refund after payout. First payouts held past the refund window.

name: Payout holds and fraud controls
what: First payout held past the refund window, minimum threshold, manual approval above a threshold Crent sets, rate limits on sign-in, checkout, export code and forms, Radar rules.
why: Under Connect Express the platform carries fraud and dispute liability.
risk: Thresholds not set.
status_note: Payout holds, thresholds, approvals and rate limits are built, with placeholder figures; no custom Radar rules.

name: Subscription pool calculation and monthly transfers
what: Month-end job closing the pool after the refund window, user-centric split by capped completed steps (as research leans), Akana share, ledger lines, transfers after a staff approval click, threshold, small-number suppression.
why: Authors will not accept a library that pays nothing. The first pool closes about a month after launch.
risk: Must be ready before the first month-end after launch (late November 2026 if launch is 26 October). Rule must be in the licence before outreach.

name: Royalty withholding and year-end summaries
what: Apply UK deduction at source on literary royalties to non-UK payees with treaty relief [check accountant]; year-end summary per payee. Manual hold until then.
why: Wrong withholding is Akana's liability.
risk: Needs gate F1 before the first overseas payout.

name: Gifts, bundles and team seats
what: Gift a workbook or membership (gift email shows a Theme only), author bundles, team seats with aggregate uptake only.
why: Seasonal and corporate revenue, not needed for first money.
risk: Employer reporting becoming staff health data. Suppression only.
status_note: Team seats exist through organisation licences (F-202) and staff can grant a gift entitlement; reader gifts and bundles are not built.

name: Workbook schema v3 with genre profiles
what: Extend workbook.schema.json: genre, language, is_demo, programme length not fixed at 12 weeks, configurable stage names, safety_tier with 'none', optional daily check, self-check and check-in, title-first fields (title, author_id, code, slug, theme_id, licence_ref, badge), stable ids on every exercise and field, author welcome note. Genre profiles set counts and required blocks: wellbeing keeps every current safety field; finance adds a no-personal-advice check; parenting keeps adults-only. Frozen by day 4.
why: The current schema assumes a 12-week wellbeing programme. Every demo workbook and every import depends on this.
risk: Changing it after demo content exists means rewriting 50 files. Freeze by day 4.

name: TypeScript validator with genre-aware claim rules
what: Port validate.py to TypeScript so the portal, build and API share one rulebook; keep Python as a CI cross-check until both agree on all 20 Maya Vaughn files. Per-genre claim allow lists, since 'improve' and 'effective' are normal in business copy. Also checks bios and listing copy.
why: The validator encodes the standing rules; reusing it is cheaper than checking every line by hand.
risk: False positives in business genres. Allow lists owned by Editorial.

name: Catalogue data model in Postgres
what: Tables for books, contributors, workbooks, versions, authors, Themes, genres and badges, carrying over AK codes, slugs, short_title, card_line and licence_ref from catalog.json and themes.json. Content served from Postgres, not static files.
why: Title-first identity and multi-author catalogues need real records.
risk: Badge honesty. Made with the author set only by the author's own sign-off.

name: Content versioning and safe updates
what: Every submit and sign-off stores an immutable snapshot with a content hash. Readers get the signed-off version. Answers attach to stable ids; ids are never reused or deleted once live (validator checks against the last live version). Removed exercises stay readable in My answers. A change to a safety line resets safety sign-off.
why: Invisible until the first author edit, then very expensive.
risk: Migration bugs losing answers. Never delete answer rows; only remap.

name: Migrate the 20 Maya Vaughn workbooks to v3
what: Convert the 20 JSON files to v3, keep exercise ids stable, load into Postgres under the Akana house organisation, run old and new validators and the parity harness.
why: The 20 are the parity test set and the first live catalogue.
risk: Breaking existing answers. Ids stable; tests before and after.

name: Themes, areas and card lines for ten new genres
what: Write Themes as shared positive shelves, areas and card lines for personal development, relationships, parenting, career, leadership, business, productivity, finance, education and life skills, in the registry with clearance status pending.
why: The library makes no sense until the new genres have shelves.
risk: Theme names not trademark cleared (gate T1). In-app only, renameable.

name: Three new field types for non-wellbeing genres
what: Number and currency fields with computed totals, a table with add-a-row (min and max rows), and a decision matrix. Each with renderer, print layout, keyboard pattern and validator rules. Dated action list and unscored knowledge check wait.
why: A finance or leadership workbook with text boxes only looks thin next to competitors.
risk: Scope creep. Capped at three. Unscored knowledge check needs Crent's view.

name: Demo flag and one-switch hide
what: is_demo on organisation, author, book and workbook. Demo items carry the Demo label, cannot be bought with real money, never enter ledger, payout, tax or funnel views, and can be hidden from the public store with one switch.
why: Invented authors must never be mistaken for real ones or earn money.
risk: Demo left live after real launch. Launch checklist item.

name: Demo catalogue: about 50 workbooks across 17 or more authors
what: Generate through the validator: at least 17 invented authors marked Demo plus a few Tier A public-domain classics, across all eleven genres. Every workbook has a listing, cover, outline and a usable Week 1; about ten are fully written. Each passes the v3 validator.
why: The store must look like a multi-author marketplace for outreach.
risk: Thin or invented-sounding content on wellbeing titles. Wellbeing demo titles stay standard tier and pass the claims check.
status_note: 50 listings are live (45 demo, 5 classics) with covers and outlines; the demo titles have no written first week yet.

name: Demo scale-up to 15 workbooks per author
what: If Crent confirms the original ask of 15 per author, extend to about 255 demo listings: listing, cover and outline only beyond the first 50, generated in batch.
why: The user's request said 15 each for at least 17 authors; the decision record says about 50. Needs confirming.
risk: Volume of thin listings makes the store look padded. Library shows depth badges.

name: Generated covers for demo and classics
what: Typographic covers generated from tokens per genre for every demo and public-domain workbook, with alt text. Real authors supply their own.
why: Every listing needs a cover; cover rights for real books are separate.
risk: Covers that imitate a real publisher's design. Plain typographic style only.

name: Public-domain file for classics
what: House-only record per classic: contributor death years with a source, edition used (never a modern reprint layout), UK, US and EU tier. Only Tier A classics clear in all three ship at launch, which avoids territory blocking.
why: Known traps: Gummere's Seneca, Giles's Art of War, The Richest Man in Babylon.
risk: Death years in research mostly marked [check]. Each verified and sourced before going live.
status_note: Records and pages exist for the 5 classics; CA, AU and NZ points are marked to confirm and no reviewer has signed.

name: Media in workbooks
what: Images, diagrams, audio and video by signed short-lived URLs, alt text, captions and transcripts required.
why: Publishers bring figures and video.
risk: Audio rights held separately.

name: Further field types and advanced logic
what: Dated action list, unscored knowledge check, carry-forward between exercises, conditional steps, reusable templates.
why: Market standard within weeks; review and migration get harder.
risk: Add only with tests.

name: Legal and trust pages
what: Reader terms, privacy notice, refund policy, cookie statement (strictly necessary only, no banner), accessibility statement, What we never collect, wellness-not-treatment statement, company details. Marketplace text marked [check legal].
why: Needed before the first payment.
risk: Company details still placeholders; mailer refuses marketing mail until the postal address is real.
status_note: Terms, privacy, cookies, refunds and the trust page are live as lawyer drafts; the accessibility statement and company details are not written.

name: Versioned terms acceptance for every party
what: Clickwrap for reader terms, author terms, publisher terms and white-label SaaS terms plus DPA and sub-processor list, with version, time and user stored like consent_versions. 15 days' notice of changes for business users. Signed PDF upload for negotiated deals.
why: No title or tenant goes live without accepted terms; P2B notice needs version history.
risk: Templates need a lawyer (gate L3). Mechanism ships with draft text; nobody signs drafts.

name: Notice and takedown flow
what: Public report form capturing DMCA 512(c)(3) and DSA Article 16 fields, queue, decision through the kill switch, statement of reasons template (DSA Article 17), counter-notice route, repeat infringer flag.
why: Rights complaints can arrive on day one once third-party books are on sale.
risk: A curated store taking a revenue share may not get DMCA safe harbour. Lawyer to confirm. Designated agent registration is a Crent task.

name: Ranking statement and business complaints route
what: Published main ranking parameters, internal complaints route for authors and publishers, reasons on suspension and notice before termination.
why: Applies if authors count as business users of an intermediary [check UK status].
risk: Low.

name: No third-party trackers by design
what: Content Security Policy that blocks third-party scripts and pixels on every host, a CI test that fails on any new external script, and no client error tracker on reader screens unless it captures no page content.
why: No ad pixels is a standing rule and a selling point; tenants will ask for pixels in week one.
risk: A marketing tool added later breaking the What we never collect page.

name: DPIA, records of processing and sub-processor list
what: Update the DPIA for marketplace, white-label (Akana as processor) and health data; records of processing; sub-processor list for the DPA.
why: Health data at scale and processor duties for tenants.
risk: Needs a privacy lawyer's read [check].

name: Adults-only confirmation
what: 18 and over confirmation at sign-up, generic sign-up screen naming no topic.
why: Wellbeing and parenting titles are written for adults.
risk: Low.

name: Repo, environments and CI
what: Private GitHub repo, Next.js App Router with TypeScript, Vercel preview and production, new Supabase project with migrations, CI running lint, type check, unit tests, validator and axe. Seed and reset scripts.
why: Day-one foundation for every stream.
risk: Vercel Pro and Supabase Pro plans needed [check costs].

name: Organisation and tenant model with RLS
what: organisations (publisher, author, white-label tenant, Akana house), org_members, tenant_id on every content, commerce and membership table from the first migration, RLS through a security definer is_member(org_id, role) reading app_metadata. Ports and rewrites migrations 001 to 009. Maya Vaughn's 20 sit under the Akana house organisation.
why: Retrofitting tenancy onto live health data is the most expensive retrofit in the build.
risk: A missed policy leaks one publisher's sales or one reader's answers.

name: Organisation roles and permissions
what: Fixed org roles: owner, editor, finance, author (own titles only), viewer. One permissions table drives RLS and the UI, with a test per role per table. No custom roles.
why: Finance must see statements but not drafts; authors only their own titles.
risk: Role sprawl. Fixed list.

name: Cross-tenant isolation and RLS test suite
what: CI tests sign in as org A and try to read and write org B's workbooks, sales, statements, members and settings, and a reader tries another tenant's entitlements. Supabase advisors in CI. Build fails on any leak.
why: The first thing a publisher asks about, and the first thing cut under pressure. It should not be.
risk: Tests only cover what they name. A test per new table.

name: Sign-in with magic link, Google and passkeys
what: Supabase Auth magic link and Google, passkeys carried over from webauthn.js. __Host- cookies. Apple sign-in once the developer account exists.
why: WCAG 2.2 Accessible Authentication favours magic links and passkeys.
risk: Magic links in spam on a new domain. SPF, DKIM, DMARC and warm-up before launch.
status_note: Magic link only; Google waits for an OAuth client and passkeys are not built.

name: Shared reader identity with per-tenant membership
what: One auth pool. A reader who signs up on a tenant site gets tenant-scoped membership, profile, consent and entitlements. Tenants see only their own members, never answers. Sign-in screen explains one login works on several sites.
why: Separate pools per tenant are a large build. Needs Crent's yes.
risk: A publisher insisting on fully separate accounts. Cut from the three weeks: target is the first signed tenant, about two weeks after launch.

name: Sealed answer storage
what: Carry over seal.ts AES-GCM sealing with AAD extended to tenant and owner id. Answers, daily checks, check-ins and self-check results sealed at rest and unsealed only server side for the owner. Seal key server side only. Autosave with last-write-wins and a visible note across two devices.
why: Health data handled as health data; the encryption wording is already published.
risk: A leaked service key or missing policy exposes health data. RLS tests and advisors before launch.

name: Private storage with signed URLs
what: Supabase Storage buckets scoped by tenant for manuscripts, signed licences, covers and exports, signed short-lived URLs, no public buckets except covers.
why: Manuscripts and contracts are confidential.
risk: A bucket left public. Advisor check.
status_note: One private org-files bucket for manuscripts and signed licences with signed links; covers are generated, not stored, and exports are streamed.

name: Feature flags and config
what: Extend app_config into flags with scope (global, tenant, workbook), server read and short cache. Used by the kill switch, launch toggles (membership, white-label, demo visible) and markets.
why: Lets unfinished parts ship switched off instead of delaying everything.
risk: Low.

name: Email system carried over with its guards
what: Port emails.ts and mailer.ts: no workbook title in reader mail (render test fails on any catalogue title), Theme only in bodies, nothing identifying in subjects, POST-only one-click unsubscribe, refusal while the postal address is a placeholder, send log, bounce and complaint suppression. Wording updated where it says 'twelve weeks'.
why: The rules are settled and coded; rewriting would reopen them.
risk: No sending domain (gate T2) or postal address blocks most mail. Decide in Week 1.
status_note: Guards, send log and one-click unsubscribe are built; bounce and complaint suppression is a hook every caller stubs, and nothing sends until Resend is set up.

name: Markets and locale data
what: Carry over markets.json and locale.js: six launch markets, currency, date formats, Help now mapping.
why: Prices, dates and Help now all read from it.
risk: Low.

name: Interface strings ready for more languages
what: All interface strings in next-intl message files with en-GB and en-US sets, Intl for dates and currency, a language field on each workbook, lang attributes on content, logical CSS properties. No translations at launch.
why: Cheap now, slow and error-prone after launch.
risk: A foreign-language wellbeing title with English-only Help now. Not live until helplines and safety review exist for that language.

name: Allowlist service worker and offline Help now page
what: Static help.html with inline CSS and tel: links for every market, precached, working signed out and offline. Worker caches only the versioned shell, help.html, fonts, icons and covers; auth callbacks, /go/, /api/, preview and token links are network only. Caches clear on sign-out. A test lists every cached URL.
why: Fixes the known fault where the current worker caches every GET, and keeps Help now reachable when the app fails.
risk: Safari sign-out clearing. Test it.

name: First-party funnel events
what: Page view, sample view, free week started, checkout started, purchase, week completed: ids and timestamps only, 13-month retention, small-number suppression downstream. No third-party analytics or replay.
why: Crent needs sales figures from day one; author dashboards read the same events.
risk: An event carrying an answer. Schema forbids free text.

name: Operational alerts and scrubbed logs
what: Email alerts to Crent on webhook failure, payout failure, email failure above a threshold and validator job errors. Logs scrubbed of form values.
why: With one operator, silent payment failures are the main way to lose money and trust.
risk: An error tracker capturing form values. Off reader screens.

name: Staff and payee sign-in hardening
what: Passkey or TOTP required for owner, finance and admin roles; re-authentication before changing payout details or domains; recovery through support with identity checks.
why: Payout detail changes are the classic fraud route on royalty platforms.
risk: Locked-out staff. Recovery route.

name: WCAG 2.2 AA build and manual pass
what: axe in CI from Week 1 on every route in both themes at 320px and 200% text. Accessible patterns for every field type, focus management between exercises, reduced motion. Manual keyboard, VoiceOver and TalkBack pass on the player in Week 3. Statement matches real results.
why: The EAA has applied to e-books and e-commerce since 28 June 2025 and publisher tenants will ask.
risk: Treating an automated pass as enough. A day of manual testing is budgeted.
status_note: Automated axe sweep on public pages in both themes and widths; the manual keyboard, VoiceOver and TalkBack pass in docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md has not been run.

name: Launch readiness and go-live checklist
what: Load test checkout and webhook in test mode, end-to-end tests for buy, membership, refund and deletion, live-mode switch, demo visibility decision, DNS and email warm-up, backups confirmed, rollback plan.
why: Sellable means it works on the day, not that the parts exist.
risk: Squeezed by slippage. Protected time in the last three days.
status_note: Checklist, rollback and backups docs and a load test script exist; live-mode switch, backups and DNS and email warm-up are not done.

name: Offline owned workbooks and drafts queue
what: Owned content cached by version, short-lived encrypted offline drafts queue, install prompt after the first win.
why: Market standard but not needed to take first money. Needs the DPIA update.
risk: Two-device conflicts.

name: Web Push reminders
what: One opt-in daily push, off by default, neutral text, quiet hours.
why: Readers will want it; the calendar covers launch.
risk: iOS supports web push only for home-screen apps [check].

name: Expanded taxonomy: 10 shelves, 51 Themes and seed migration
what: Load the draft taxonomy (docs/research/taxonomy.json, categories.md) into content/registry: 3 new shelves (Health and Body, Faith and Spirituality, Creativity and Making) beside the 7 seeded, 7 new areas, and 34 new Themes beside the 17 existing, each with clearance_status pending and min_books 3. Fill line and topics for the five Mind and Mood Themes, add the extra hidden topics to existing Themes, move stoicism from Chosen Habits to Wisdom for Living. Optional additive migration adding themes.group_suitable boolean not null default false. Regenerate the seed. All 17 existing ids kept.
why: Research found 13 of Blinkist's 31 categories with no Akana home, including faith, health, creativity and communication. The new catalogue titles need these Themes to exist before they can be seeded.
risk: None of the 34 new names has had a register search (gate T1); they stay in-app and renameable. The hidden-topic leak test must cover the new condition words (depression, OCD, PTSD, debt, divorce). Migration number is the next free one at merge, which shifts the 0013 to 0022 numbers in akana-business.md. Update 7 October 2026: Reading Scripture (reading-scripture) is retired because Bible study is out of scope for now; migration 0025 adds themes.status and marks it retired, and the id is never reused. 50 Themes are active.

name: Optional faith genre
what: Append 'faith' to GENRES in packages/schema/src/v3.ts (append only), add it to content/registry/genres.json and a genre profile in @akana/validate with its own rules: no healing or answered-prayer claims, a pastoral signpost beside Help now, and a scripture licence check. New additive migration that drops and recreates the genres CHECK from 0002 with 12 ids, then inserts the row; 0002 itself is not edited. Add the GENRE_LABELS entry in apps/web/app/publish/options.ts. Make scripts/check-registry.ts throw on an unknown genre instead of treating it as wellbeing. Built only if Crent says yes.
why: None of the 11 genres fits prayer and devotional titles. Faith titles need their own guardrails, and a genre is what the consent screen and the release gate can key on. Adding a genre value is additive under the freeze.
risk: supabase/tests/0002_catalogue.sql asserts exactly 11 genres (line 109) and fails once a 12th is seeded. It must change in the same pull request. F-221 covers faith titles and licences after launch; this entry is only the code change.

name: Faith consent screen
what: Explicit, versioned consent before a reader's first faith-genre workbook, built like the health data consent (F-026) and recorded with its own version. Withdrawing it in You stops new saves in faith titles. The wording says that using a faith title can reveal religious belief and that answers stay sealed.
why: Religious belief is special category data. Akana is not a religious body, so it cannot rely on Article 9(2)(d) and needs explicit consent under 9(2)(a), as for health [check legal].
risk: Consent wording and the privacy notice line about religious belief do not need lawyer review now (Crent, 7 October 2026): closed. If Crent declines the faith genre, the trigger must key on the Faith and Spirituality shelf instead. F-215 extends the same consent to church-run groups after launch.

name: Bible quotation support and attribution
what: Quotation support only, inside Bible-based faith titles (devotional, prayer, character, practical and Christian living). Not a Bible study feature: since 7 October 2026 no title is built around studying or reading through Scripture. World English Bible as the default quotation text: the British Edition (WEBBE) for en-GB workbooks, the WEB for en-US, and the WEBBE with the Deuterocanon for Catholic and Orthodox titles. Optional scripture_text field on the workbook (additive). Attribution line on the Start or notes screen, for example 'Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible British Edition, which is in the public domain.' Validator rule: WEB wording is never edited, each quotation is marked when a workbook uses more than one version, and licensed versions keep a verse counter against the publisher's limit. No reading plans, passage-by-passage study screens or commentary features.
why: Bible-based titles quote Scripture. The King James Version is under Crown rights in the UK and needs Cambridge University Press permission for commercial use. Modern versions such as the NIV and ESV carry verse and percentage limits. The WEB is public domain with no limit. Crent decided on 7 October 2026 that Bible study is out of scope for now, so this entry covers quotations only.
risk: KJV wording quoted inside a public-domain classic (Bunyan, Spurgeon, Ryle) may still need Cambridge's permission in the UK [check legal]. en-AU, en-CA and en-NZ editions are not settled [check]. 'World English Bible' is a trade mark, so a changed text cannot carry the name.

name: Public-domain house records for the new classics
what: One house record in docs/public-domain/ and a page at /public-domain/<code> for each of the 50 new classics in the catalogue research (29 faith, 7 growth, 7 learning, 4 work and money, 3 mind and health). Each names the edition, every author, translator and editor with a sourced death year, the UK, US and IE conclusion, the Tier (A or B) and the reviewer. First batch in week 2: the titles Crent picks for v2 seeding, led by the classics that open a hidden Theme. The rest follow as content-track work.
why: No classic goes live without a signed record (F-118). Edition traps are real: Gutenberg #5657 Brother Lawrence is a copyrighted 2002 edition, Gummere's Seneca is in UK copyright to 2039, and Franklin's #20203 has an editor with no known death year.
risk: Canada, Australia and New Zealand terms are still [to confirm]. Three classics are Tier B (In His Steps, How We Think, The Elements of Style) and stay off sale at launch. Scientific Advertising has no Gutenberg text and needs a transcription from a 1923 scan. Each record waits for a named reviewer.
status_note: 50 records are drafted (33 ready for a signer, 17 need a check); none is signed and their workbooks are not seeded.

name: Demo Catalogue v2 seeding
what: Merge the five catalogue research files into docs/planning/AK_Demo_Catalogue_v2.json after Crent approves (merge plan in docs/research/catalogue/SUMMARY.md), then point the seed builder at it. 120 new listings (70 demo, 50 classics; the four Reading Scripture demo titles were removed on 7 October 2026 and are skipped) at first-week depth with covers, outlines and card lines. Normalise genre, safety profile, advice note, area and depth values; one author record per person; final codes after a collision check. Demo titles load live with the Demo badge; classics load as draft until their record is signed; faith titles load only after the faith genre decision.
why: Every one of the 50 active Themes reaches three titles on paper, so every shelf can look stocked. It also gives Akana Business and church prospects something to browse.
risk: Title checks unfinished on several demo titles. With classics in draft, 25 of the 50 active Themes stay below three live titles and so stay hidden. Seed size grows past the SQL editor limit again, so loading needs the batch script.
status_note: Approved by Crent on 8 October 2026. seed.sql is built from v2 and keeps a title's status on re-run. New titles load as draft and go live through release_version.

name: New support signposts
what: Five new signpost groups in content/catalog/support_lines.json, by market and with a checked date: money_worries_lines (free debt and money help), eating_support_lines (food and eating), bereavement_support_lines, new_parent_support_lines and carer_support_lines. Shown beside Help now on the titles that name them, as when_home_is_not_safe and family_support_lines are today. Signposts only: no claim of endorsement or partnership.
why: Twelve new titles name one of these groups: debt titles, food planning, grief, new babies and caring. Readers on those titles may be under strain.
risk: Only money_worries_lines has draft entries, for GB (MoneyHelper, StepChange, National Debtline, Citizens Advice) and IE (MABS), and their numbers and hours are not yet verified. Any group not checked by market is set to null before seeding.

name: Theological reviewer workflow
what: A Theological Reviewer sign-off kind in the release gate. A faith-genre workbook cannot move from in_review to approved without it, recorded against the content hash with the reviewer's name, tradition and date in the internal block. The reviewer approves the tradition label (Protestant, Catholic, Orthodox, General Christian) and the line 'Written from within the [tradition] tradition. Readers from other churches are welcome.' A title labelled for one tradition needs a reviewer from that tradition. Safety copy stays with the Clinical Safety Lead.
why: One reviewer cannot speak for every church, and the classics carry doctrinal sensitivities (Bunyan's Giant Pope, MacDonald on atonement, Catholic sacramental practice in Kempis Book 4 and Ignatius).
risk: No reviewer is named. Without one, no faith title can release. Buddhist and Hindu classics need their own reviewers.

name: Customer organisation kinds and profile
what: New organisation kinds business, church, charity and community_group (migration widens the organisations.kind check). Profile with billing contact, VAT number, charity number and size band. Staff create them from /admin/organisations.
why: Businesses, churches and small groups want Akana for their people. Today organisations can only be the house, publishers, author companies or individuals.
risk: Part of the manual-sales pilot (F-201 to F-206), which only fits if it runs as an extra stream from week 2. Crent's call.

name: Organisation licences and seats with team_seat entitlement
what: Seat count, title scope, start and end. Claiming a seat writes a library-wide team_seat entitlement; releasing it ends the entitlement and leaves the work read only. has_entitlement respects the licence's title scope.
why: Buyers pay per seat or by band. The team_seat source is already reserved in 0004.
risk: Replaces app.has_entitlement, the most important access function. Needs a full RLS test pass.

name: Invitations and seat claim
what: Email invite with a hashed token, accepted only on a button press (the 0012 pattern), 18+ confirmation, link to an existing account. Send limits. The email names the organisation, never a title.
why: Members need a safe way in that the organisation controls.
risk: An invite email naming a wellbeing title would disclose health data. The render test applies.

name: Minimal organisation console: seats and invitations
what: Invite, resend, revoke and release a seat. Counts: seats bought, claimed and people started. Suppressed under the owner threshold.
why: The buyer needs to see uptake. Counts are enough.
risk: Small groups make counts identifying. Suppression under suppression_threshold_owner (5) applies.

name: Organisation terms, DPA and privacy notice section
what: Drafts for the lawyer: organisation terms (adults only, no access to answers, no compulsion for wellbeing), the DPA, and a privacy notice section on joining through an organisation.
why: The organisation is controller of the roster and Akana its processor; Akana stays an independent controller of each member's own work [check legal].
risk: No organisation goes live until the lawyer approves the text (O10).

name: Akana for organisations page
what: 'Talk to us' until prices are set. States the privacy line. No church claims until faith titles exist.
why: Outreach needs a page to point at.
risk: Copy promising church content before any faith title is released.

name: Groups with leaders
what: Create a group, pick one title and pin its version, assign a leader and co-leader, add members from seat holders or by invitation. Group name warning for sensitive words.
why: Churches, book clubs and workplace cohorts do one workbook together.
risk: A group name such as 'Anxiety support, Finance team' puts health data in the roster.

name: Group schedule and soft pace
what: Start date, unit open dates, meeting time. 'Your group is on unit 3' on Home and Today. Calendar file (reuses F-024).
why: A group needs to know which unit it is on this week.
risk: Drifting into streaks or 'behind' labels. The 0003 rule (no streak or missed-day derivation) applies to groups.

name: Facilitator guides
what: Separate Zod schema in packages/schema, validator rules (claim words, Help now on wellbeing), editing through the staff JSON editor (F-086), review and sign-off, leader view per unit, print view.
why: A guide saves the leader preparing and keeps sessions consistent.
risk: The licence must allow guides as derived material. Who writes them is Crent's call.

name: Group check-ins
what: Fixed choices only, member-controlled sharing, off by default in workplace groups. No free text column exists.
why: A light weekly signal for the leader without exposing anyone's work.
risk: Shared free text between members would likely bring Akana into Online Safety Act user-to-user scope [check legal].

name: Aggregate organisation reports
what: Monthly counts per licence and per group above threshold. CSV. No names against progress. pgTAP tests prove leaders and owners cannot read answers or private check-ins.
why: HR and church leaders need evidence the spend was used.
risk: Counts per wellbeing title can reveal health data. Shown only above the threshold.

name: Faith consent screen
what: Explicit consent for faith titles and church groups, versioned, withdrawable. Needs a faith genre first (F-221).
why: Membership of a church group and use of a faith title both reveal religious belief [check legal].
risk: Overlaps F-150, which brings the faith-title consent forward to week 2. If F-150 ships, this entry reduces to extending it to church-run groups.

name: Report a concern
what: From any group screen to Akana support, with the safeguarding-lead prompt for church groups.
why: Church safeguarding guidance asks for a clear route for concerns.
risk: Akana support is not a safeguarding service. The prompt must send people to their church's safeguarding lead.

name: Organisation billing on Stripe
what: Seat quantity, church bands, group per-member plans, invoices with 30-day terms, Bacs, tax ids, scheduled seat falls, dunning. Organisation subscription mirror separate from reader subscriptions.
why: Removes the manual invoice and bulk grant (C10) once volume justifies it.
risk: VAT on overseas churches and charities that are not in business [check accountant].
status_note: Seat subscriptions, invoices on 30-day terms and Bacs are built in Stripe test mode only; organisation prices are unset (N2).

name: Faith genre and first licensed Christian titles
what: New genre with guardrails, Themes and author outreach. Content, licences and review, not only code. Blocks the church offer.
why: Churches can only use general titles until Christian titles are licensed.
risk: Overlaps F-149, which brings the genre code change forward to week 2. If F-149 ships, this entry is the licensing and content work only.

name: Pool and ledger for organisation income
what: Source field on ledger and pool lines, the church per-reader split, author statements that do not name the organisation.
why: Organisation income feeds the D3 pool and must be shown apart from reader memberships.
risk: An author learning that a named employer runs a wellbeing title [check legal].

name: Private organisation tenants with branding
what: Tenant kind organisation, invite only, no checkout. Waits on A7 and the tenant sign-in decision.
why: Larger buyers want their own look and host.
risk: Sealing binds answers to the tenant, so work on the marketplace cannot move to a branded tenant later. Decide the tenant when the organisation starts.

name: Held pace
what: Optional: units open when the group reaches them. Changes has_entitlement; needs a full RLS test pass.
why: Some leaders want the group on the same unit.
risk: A small, risky change to the most important access function.

name: Join links and CSV bulk invite
what: Join code with optional email domain restriction. CSV upload with validation.
why: Large rosters are slow to invite one by one.
risk: A leaked join code admitting people outside the organisation. Domain restriction and seat caps limit it.

name: Self-serve sign-up for Group and small Teams plans
what: Card checkout, the organiser becomes owner.
why: Small groups will not wait for a sales call.
risk: Group organisers are usually consumers, so DMCC Act subscription rules apply [check legal].
status_note: Built behind the org_self_serve flag, which is off until organisation prices are set.

name: SAML SSO for organisation members
what: Large employers only.
why: A named large prospect may require it to sign [check].
risk: Built for one prospect's identity provider and hard to generalise.

name: Organisation offboarding and export
what: Roster and invoices out, roster deleted, members told their work is still theirs. Never answers.
why: The DPA requires deletion at the end of the contract.
risk: An export path that reaches answers. None may exist.
